definitions.explanation: The spirit of a deceased person who harbors deep resentment and returns to the world of the living to cause harm, disaster, or misfortune. A fundamental concept in Japanese folk religion and a recurring motif in Japanese literature and horror.

examples.japanese: {怨霊|おんりょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{取|と}り{憑|つ}かれた→取り憑く：11969_toritsuku⟧。
examples.english: I was possessed by a vengeful spirit.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天変地異|てんぺんちい}→天変地異：06146_tenpenchii⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{怨霊|おんりょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{祟|たた}り→祟り：22000_tatari⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{恐|おそ}れられた→恐れる：02023_osoreru⟧。
examples.english: Natural disasters were feared to be the curse of vengeful spirits.

examples.japanese: {菅原道真|すがわらのみちざね}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{怨霊|おんりょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ひとり⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{後|のち}→後：03545_nochi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{天神|てんじん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧{祀|まつ}られた。
examples.english: Sugawara no Michizane is one of Japan's most famous vengeful spirits, and was later enshrined as the deity Tenjin.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Belief in {怨霊|おんりょう} has been a powerful force in Japanese history and culture. When powerful or unjustly treated people died with grudges, their spirits were believed to cause plagues, natural disasters, and political upheaval. To appease them, they were often enshrined as deities ({御霊|ごりょう}⟦{信仰|しんこう}→信仰：03685_shinkou⟧, goryo shinko). Famous historical {怨霊|おんりょう} include {菅原道真|すがわらのみちざね}, {平将門|たいらのまさかど}, and {崇徳天皇|すとくてんのう}.

Do not confuse with the homophone ⟦{音量|おんりょう}→音量：10009_onryou⟧ (volume, loudness), which uses different kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {怨霊|おんりょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{祟|たた}り→祟り：22000_tatari⟧: curse of a vengeful spirit
- {怨霊|おんりょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{鎮|しず}める→鎮める：29400_shizumeru⟧: to pacify a vengeful spirit
- {怨霊|おんりょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{取|と}り{憑|つ}かれる→取り憑く：11969_toritsuku⟧: to be possessed by a vengeful spirit
